title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 237 (Power of Central Government to provide for amalgamation of companies in public interest)

content.overview: Section 237 empowers the Central Government, where it is satisfied that it is essential in the public interest that two or more companies should amalgamate, to provide by order for the amalgamation of those companies into a single company. A copy of the proposed order is served so that the company may be heard. The order provides for the transfer of property, rights and liabilities, and for continuation of proceedings. An appeal lies as the section states. This is a Central Government-driven public-interest amalgamation, distinct from a member-driven scheme under section 232.
content.glance: CG satisfied amalgamation is essential in public interest → may order amalgamation of two or more companies; company heard on proposed order; transfer of property/liabilities; appeal as provided; distinct from s. 232 member-driven scheme.
content.study: Where the Central Government is satisfied that it is essential in the public interest that two or more companies should amalgamate, it may provide by order for amalgamation of those companies into a single company with such constitution, property, powers, rights, interests, authorities and privileges, and with such liabilities, duties and obligations, as may be specified. A copy of the proposed order is sent in draft to each company concerned so that it may be heard. Current-law framing: establish CG’s satisfaction that amalgamation is essential in public interest; draft order and hearing opportunity for the companies; final order effecting transfer of property and liabilities; note appeal rights. Distinct from Tribunal-sanctioned member schemes under s. 232 and from fast-track s. 233.

sections.heading: Public-Interest Condition
sections.body: Central Government must be satisfied that amalgamation of two or more companies is essential in the public interest.

sections.heading: Order and Hearing
sections.body: CG may provide by order for amalgamation; draft of proposed order is given so that each company may be heard.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Order provides for constitution of the amalgamated company and transfer of property, rights, liabilities and continuation of proceedings as specified.

sections.heading: Appeal and Distinction
sections.body: Appeal lies as the section provides; distinct from member-driven s. 232 schemes.

provisions.title: Power of Central Government to provide for amalgamation of companies in public interest

examples.title: Public-interest amalgamation
examples.body: The Central Government, satisfied that amalgamation of two companies in a critical sector is essential in the public interest, issues a draft order under s. 237, hears the companies, and then orders amalgamation with transfer of property and liabilities.

examples.title: Not a substitute for s. 232
examples.body: Members cannot treat s. 237 as an optional alternative to a voluntary s. 232 scheme. Section 237 is available only when the Central Government is satisfied that amalgamation is essential in the public interest.

hypotheticals.question: Can the Central Government order amalgamation under s. 237 for purely private commercial convenience without a public-interest basis?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 237 requires the Central Government to be satisfied that amalgamation is essential in the public interest. It is not a general power to impose private mergers.

distinctions.title: CG public-interest amalgamation (s. 237) vs Tribunal merger scheme (s. 232)
distinctions.left: CG order when essential in public interest; companies heard on draft order
distinctions.right: Member/creditor-driven scheme; Tribunal sanction under ss. 230–232

misconceptions.trap: Section 237 is just another way for companies to merge without Tribunal process whenever they prefer.
misconceptions.correction: Section 237 is available only when the Central Government is satisfied that amalgamation is essential in the public interest. Ordinary voluntary mergers use ss. 230–233.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 237 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Test public-interest satisfaction of CG. II. Draft order and hearing. III. Effect of order. IV. Distinguish s. 232. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Public-interest basis; draft order; hearing; transfer terms; precise relief.

examTips: CG order after hearing on draft.
